documents.title: Paperhands
documents.text:
An agent-first Rust binary for an autonomous trading research system, inspired
by Andrej Karpathy's [autoresearch](https://github.com/karpathy/autoresearch).
Planned venues include Polymarket, Robinhood and other platforms. The trading
specification is pending.

documents.title: Paperhands
documents.text:
Version 0.1.0 is a working CLI scaffold: semantic command discovery, bundled
documentation and an automatically maintained agent skill. It has no market
connections, credentials, backtests, experiment runner or order execution.

documents.title: CLI principles
documents.text:
- Semantic help uses our `clap-how-to` crate, following the discovery pattern
  used by Cloudflare's `cf` CLI, Ontology and ICQ.
- All output is JSON by default, including help, version and errors.
  `--human` explicitly selects readable text.
- Commands, documentation, prepared embeddings and the Paperhands agent skill
  travel inside one binary. Semantic help runs offline.
- Every invocation installs or repairs the bundled skill at
  `~/.agents/skills/paperhands/SKILL.md`. Changed bundled files are replaced even
  if edited locally or installed by a different version. Keep personal additions
  in separate files. `PAPERHANDS_SKILLS_DIR` overrides the skill directory itself.

documents.title: CLI principles
documents.text: See [the CLI contract](docs/cli.md) and [the bundled skill](skills/paperhands/SKILL.md).

documents.title: Develop
documents.text:
```sh
cargo run --example prepare_help
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --locked
cargo publish --dry-run --locked
```

documents.title: Develop
documents.text:
Regenerate `assets/how-to.json` after changing commands, README, CLI docs or the
skill. Source-freshness tests catch stale indexes. The query encoder and model
attribution are supplied by `clap-how-to` and its `pocket-encoder` dependency
(MIT code; Apache-2.0 model/tokenizer). Use `paperhands docs read cli` for details.

documents.title: Discover commands by intent
documents.text:
Search accepts one quoted question, 1..512 UTF-8 bytes without control characters,
and returns at most five source matches. Scores rank sources; they are not
probabilities. The model has a 128-token context and can return unrelated matches.
Search retrieves existing help and documentation; it does not generate answers
or execute suggested commands. Command results include an exact help invocation;
document results identify a bundled source, section and one-based line.

documents.title: Read documentation
documents.text:
`paperhands docs list` returns guide IDs. `paperhands docs read ID` reads bundled
text selected by ID: `overview`, `cli` or `skill`. These are versioned snapshots
inside the executable, not arbitrary filesystem paths or live websites.

documents.title: Output
documents.text:
Every successful invocation writes one JSON object to stdout with `schema`,
`version`, `ok`, `command` and `data`. Help and version follow the same contract.
Errors write one JSON object to stderr, leave stdout empty and exit nonzero.
Syntax and input errors exit 2; runtime failures exit 1. Add global `--human`
before or after a subcommand for readable output. No command launches a pager.

documents.title: Agent skill lifecycle
documents.text:
On every invocation, before command execution, Paperhands compares its embedded
skill with `~/.agents/skills/paperhands/SKILL.md` and atomically replaces missing
or different contents. This includes first run, help and version. The executable
is authoritative even after a downgrade. Unchanged files are not rewritten;
unrelated files are retained. The managed skill file may not be a symlink.
An installation failure exits with a structured error instead of claiming success.

documents.title: Agent skill lifecycle
documents.text:
Set `PAPERHANDS_SKILLS_DIR` to override the complete destination directory.
`paperhands skills` returns the installed directory, bundled content and refresh
result. No harness settings or external skill files are modified. Harnesses that
discover `~/.agents/skills` directly or through symlinks can load this skill.

documents.title: Current capabilities
documents.text:
`paperhands status` reports `stage: scaffold`, `trading_enabled: false` and the
planned venues. Polymarket and Robinhood are intended integrations only. This
release cannot place orders, access accounts or claim experiment results.

documents.title: Bundled model attribution
documents.text:
The semantic encoder comes from [clap-how-to](https://github.com/Gonzih/clap-how-to)
and [pocket-encoder](https://crates.io/crates/pocket-encoder). Encoder code is MIT;
model and tokenizer are Apache-2.0, with upstream provenance, license and NOTICE
bundled in that dependency. The upstream model is
[sentence-transformers/paraphrase-MiniLM-L3-v2](https://huggingface.co/sentence-transformers/paraphrase-MiniLM-L3-v2).
Search JSON includes the exact encoder fingerprint and model identity.

documents.title: Paperhands
documents.text:
Start with `paperhands status` to inspect this binary's actual capabilities.
Version 0.1.0 is a scaffold; trading, backtesting and venue integrations await
the operator's specification. Do not report planned capabilities as implemented.

documents.title: Paperhands
documents.text:
JSON is the default for results, help, version and errors. Use `--human` only
when readable text is requested. Search is offline semantic retrieval using
`clap-how-to`; inspect the cited source or command help before choosing an action.
Search never executes a result and does not generate an answer.

documents.title: Paperhands
documents.text:
The binary installs and refreshes this managed file on every invocation.
Local edits are overwritten. Keep personal additions in separate files.
`PAPERHANDS_SKILLS_DIR` overrides the complete skill directory; the default is
`~/.agents/skills/paperhands`. Run `paperhands skills` to inspect installation.
